title: A month after Paramount acquired Warner Bros. Discovery, its merged game division is laying people off
summary: Skydance Games has "made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects."
body: Just over a month after Paramount closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery and renamed itself as Skydance, the company's games division has laid off an unspecified number of employees. Reports of the cuts first surfaced earlier today on LinkedIn, where multiple employees reported being let go. Lead engineer David Vera , who was not among those put out of work, said the studio "lost a ton of great talent," while another post by principal environment artist Dana Klaren listed more than 25 people who'd been let go, including himself. Senior gameplay and game AI programmer Rebecca Vessal said in her own message that "most" of her team had been let go. Prior to their merger, both Paramount and Warner had their own game divisions: Paramount actually had two, Skydance Interactive and Skydance New Media, which were mashed together into Skydance Games Studio earlier this year. The merged company announced that it will be publishing PlatinumGames' upcoming Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin; Skydance New Media is also working on Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra , although the current status of that game is unclear. title: Take-Two expects to make as much as $3.5 billion during the GTA 6 launch period
summary: Pre-orders for GTA 6 are still "unprecedented," says the publisher.
body: GTA publisher Take-Two projects net bookings (total completed sales, essentially) of $3.35 to $3.5 billion for its current Q3 2027 financial quarter, "driven by the groundbreaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6" in a little over a week. "The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is ten days away and, with pre-orders continuing to reach unprecedented levels, we expect to deliver an historic year for our company," said Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick. The publisher has previously said that it doesn't want to reveal the total number of GTA 6 preorders because "the raw numbers could potentially be misleading," given that it's never seen numbers like these before. The $3.35 to $3.5 billion net bookings expectation for the GTA 6 launch period is actually slightly below analyst expectations of $3.51 billion, as compiled by LSEG Data & Analytics (via Reuters ). Take-Two's net bookings for its previous financial quarter, Q2 2027, came in below expectations at $1.60 billion, and 18% drop year-over-year. NBA 2K7 was one of the culprits there. title: Cheaper OLEDs may be here even quicker than we thought as TCL CSOT says its new inkjet printing facility could be up and running as soon as this time next year
summary: Previous rumours had it penned for 2028.
body: TCL CSOT (the subsidiary of TCL that manufactures OLEDs and other panels) says its new inkjet-printed OLED factory has "entered the equipment move-in phase" (via TechPowerUp ) after the project "progressed at a rapid pace". In other words, it's started filling up its production facility with the equipment to produce inkjet OLEDs. Production, the company says, is targeted for about this time next year. What's the big deal, you ask? It all comes down to that phrase, "inkjet-printed". Inkjet printing (IJP) should be a much more cost-effective way of making OLED panels, which means it should ultimately deliver OLED gaming monitors that are cheaper than traditionally manufactured ones. Which is saying something, considering how much traditionally manufactured OLEDs have dropped in price over the past year—you can currently pick up a 240 Hz OLED monitor for just $269 at Walmart , for instance. Having OLEDs even cheaper than this will be a whirlwind of fresh air in the current very expensive PC hardware market. IJP should give us such cheaper panels because the way it makes OLEDs doesn't involve as much wastage. Normally, you have some OLED materials moving through a mask, and some of th…

title: Great news! Nier: Automata's install size is no longer 7x bigger than it should be (it was 366 GB)
summary: 2B, times 183, plus G.
body: Last Friday, the very good RPG Nier: Automata underwent what the scientific community calls 'puffer-fishification'. That is to say, it suddenly and inexplicably ballooned to over 700% of its original download size, as an update magically transformed the game from a reedy 50 GB lightweight into a 366-GB behemoth. But it has since hit the Ozempic and is now back down to its regular size. "We have identified the cause and now resolved this issue," tweeted the official Nier X account earlier today. "Apologies for any inconvenience caused." Notably absent from the bugfix notice was any explanation as to just what had happened. It might be academic at this point, but I for one would love to know how you accidentally make a game seven times bigger without anything changing. Squenix is keeping schtum, but Rick Lane suggested, in our article last week about the bug, that it might have been related to Nier: Automata's DLC packages. "When selected for download on Steam, each DLC appears to have the same file size as the base game", he noted. "Weirdly though, this is only true for the initial download and installation. title: World of Warcraft: Forever bumps dungeon XP from monsters by 50% after some community feedback I will diplomatically call passionate
summary: Back on that grindset.
body: World of Warcraft: Forever made some changes to how dungeons work—rather than getting a bunch of XP from enemies in dungeons, you predominantly get experience points from the quests surrounding them. Which is made slightly better for the fact that there are just more dungeons overall —so while you can't sit in dungeons until level 60, you can chain between those dungeons with minimal questing, though some questing is still basically mandatory if you care about being efficient. This has been a point of consternation. Any brief visit over to the r/classicwow subreddit leads to a raft of complaint threads about dungeon XP , though other communities do vary. It should be mentioned that a singular subreddit isn't reflective of the game's entire population, mind—but it is notable how upset the dungeon-loving slice of WoW's playerbase is. To try and soothe that ache, Blizzard's gone ahead and buffed the XP gain : "At about 11:05 PST today, we deployed a hotfix that increased kill experience in dungeons by 50%, so it feels better to go back in for more runs," writes community manager Kaivax. body: Tomorrow, November 10, EVE Online is releasing a new expansion, Fractured Skies , and companion FPS EVE Vanguard is going into something Fenris Creations is calling a 24/7 alpha. Formal early access on Steam is coming late next year, but you can buy the game and play it through EVE's own client⁠ —and it won't go away like prior playtests. Tomorrow will also see Vanguard start to fulfill its promise as a linked game to EVE Online⁠—completing contracts in the multiplayer FPS will create military campaign opportunities players can find and act on in EVE—marking the return of a dream Fenris (formerly CCP Games) has pursued since the ill-fated PS3 shooter, Dust 514 . I sat down with Vanguard game director Scott Davis and EVE design director Greg Hennessey to talk about what's coming tomorrow and further down the line. From a pure gameplay perspective, Davis told me that NPC AI and new player onboarding are the biggest improvements in Vanguard since its last playtest . The NPC enemies inhabiting Vanguard's levels just weren't challenging enough, and while it's easy to make them better shots, the problem was more one of tactical depth. title: Inspired by Dark Messiah and Thief, this stealth game sees you sneak through a medieval megastructure prowled by undead guards
summary: The Citadel Project will be released next week.
body: It's a great time to be a fan of both Thief: The Dark Project and Dark Messiah of Might and Magic . A Thief remaster from Nightdive—which features a new campaign—is coming next month , while Dark Messiah is getting a Ubisoft-approved community edition that adds co-op, new modes and more. There are also numerous spiritual successors in the works for both games, such as the dark and Thief-y Gloomwood and the Dark Messiah-inspired Fatekeeper and Alkahest . Until earlier today, I hadn't seen a game inspired by both Thief and Dark Messiah at the same time (apart from Dishonored , I suppose, though that was made by Dark Messiah developers Arkane, so I'm not sure that counts). But that all changed when The Citadel Project snuck through my eyes and booted my ignorance right out of my brain. Created by solo outfit Reliquary Software, The Citadel Project synthesises the designs of Thief and Dark Messiah with first-person indie gaming's current fascination with megastructures. It casts you as a sickle-wielding prisoner trying to escape a sprawling medieval fortress prowled by shambling undead guards. The Citadel Project's Thief leanings are most obvious at a glance. title: WoW: Forever is more than just a millennial retirement home
summary: Though bingo night IS poppin'.
body: Play This Right Now Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday. World of Warcraft: Forever is fascinating from so many perspectives—not necessarily in terms of what's on offer (it is, despite my enamorment, still very much Classic WoW) but in what it means for the MMO genre at large. It's the kind of project that usually only gets cooked up in "what ifs", a version of a 20-year old game that decided not to go for expansions, but to instead spread out horizontally . A World of Warcraft that didn't have to rush a single hour of development time. It's an attempt at not only just recreating nostalgia, but applying a fine layer of polish to that nostalgia. Forever has over 1,000 new quests and dungeons —and having played some of them in my 50 hours with its beta, I can say that Blizzard has absolutely nailed what I've seen so far. body: Deadline reports that a Canadian documentary about the history of BioWare was already two years into filming when EA closed the studio. Now, it's becoming a sad goodbye to a legendary developer. "The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes," the documentary's writer and director Akash Sherman said. "It's a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio's recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction." The documentary, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, features interviews with the studio's founders, Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, as well as developers Casey Hudson, Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen, and Caroline Livingstone, voice actor Jennifer Hale, former CEO of EA John Riccitello, and vice president of Lucasfilm Games Douglas Reilly. "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and genuinely moved," Muzyka and Zeschuk said in a statement. title: After seeing them myself, I'm convinced WoW: Forever's RP servers don't need to be this separate, and I say that as a decorated veteran of MMO roleplay
summary: I'm kinda just playing chiller PvE, here.
body: I've been stuck into World of Warcraft: Forever —at the time of writing, I'm around 15 hours /played (and will likely be 20+ hours by the time you're reading this) on my warrior. I chose the roleplay ruleset because, well, I'm a roleplayer. I've been writing and being cringe in videogames for over 15 years . RP in WoW is, actually, what got me into writing in the first place. My clear and obvious mastery over the written word was hard-won by being a terribly annoying edgelord death knight, for which I apologise. I was curious about the implementation of the roleplay ruleset back when it was properly announced—back then, I thought it was great that we're being given our own place, but being completely split off from "normal" ruleset (which I'll be calling PvE for simplicity) didn't seem necessary to me. Having played in the roleplay ruleset for a little while, my opinion has only been vindicated. Splitting PvE and PvP rulesets does make sense. For instance, a resource node might be easier to gather on PvE, throwing the economic balance of the PvP server out of the window. But beyond technical limitations, a complete, strict divide between RP and PvE just has me scratching my head. …

title: What's the toughest choice you've made in an RPG?
summary: Unburden yourself.
body: Dungeon Master (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Dungeon Master , PC Gamer's regular RPG column, where Online Editor Fraser Brown delves into PC gaming's most beloved and enduring genre. Grab a seat in our badly-lit tavern and please ignore the goblin puke. We love a big RPG dilemma, don't we? Right up until the point where we actually have to make the choice and we stare at our screens for an uncomfortably long time, hoping we'll figure out a way to make a call and not feel absolutely terrible about it later. For my money, the best—agonising, guilt-inducing—choices are the really personal ones. I love that Mass Effect lets me determine the fate of the galaxy in all these different ways, but it never gives me a reason to care about the rachni, for instance, or the council, so when I have to decide to save them or let them die, it becomes more of an abstract moral choice. Disco Elysium , then, left me in tatters. It's more personal and intimate than a productive therapy session. There's a card you can read pretty early on, stuck inside a ledger, that opens the wound that Harry worked very hard—by abusing alcohol and drugs—to forget. If you toss it, you never get it back. title: Todd Howard's game design power is knowing when to make things 'simple and digestible' according to Skyrim's lead designer

body: Todd Howard is one of the most recognisable names in game development, yet despite this, the Bethesda director's overarching thoughts on game design remain something of an enigma. Howard has admitted that he doesn't like talking about his games. As such, we rarely get much insight into his broader design philosophy. Yet according to Bruce Nesmith, lead designer of Skyrim , Howard certainly has a specific set of skills when it comes to game design. In a wide-ranging interview with The Examined Game , Nesmith discussed his time working with Bethesda. During the chat, Nesmith was asked what it was like working with Howard, and he credited Howard with a knack for seeing things from the player's point of view: "Part of what Todd has, historically for Skyrim and Fallout 3 and everything, been very good at is putting himself in the seat of your typical player," Nesmith explained. "As a developer, I sit in an ivory tower. It's inescapable … I think more deeply about games, definitely, than your typical player. title: Nier: Automata developer is 'currently investigating' a bizarre update bug that drastically inflated the game's file size from 50GB to 366GB
summary: Square Enix is 'working to resolve the issue'.
body: Usually, it's a good thing when a patch makes an already excellent game substantially larger. But in the case of Nier: Automata 's most recent update, bigger is most certainly not better. On Friday, the beloved action RPG from Square Enix received what should have been a straightforward update to add localisation support for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Korean languages. But as reported by Automaton Media, the update also increased the game's file size from 50 gigabytes to a staggering 366 (and a half) gigabytes. "We have identified an issue following the latest update for Nier: Automata … where installation requires significantly more storage space than intended," wrote Square Enix in a Steam post . "We are currently investigating the cause and working to resolve the issue. We apologise for the inconvenience." It isn't clear how this issue has occurred, but it may be related to Nier: Automata's DLC. When selected for download on Steam, each DLC appears to have the same file size as the base game. title: It's hard to meet women when I keep teleporting all the time
summary: This is why there's a male loneliness epidemic.
body: Los Santos Customs I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier . Am I cheating? I might be cheating. I did not actually install a new mod for today's iteration of Los Santos Customs.
